findings.title: DECISIONS-r3 Q1 ('keeps v1 #529') gives no exception for Gemini, but TECH-SPEC's own evidence (now confirmed by direct source read) shows the matcher cannot ever fire on Gemini CLI
findings.claim: Q1 settles external-MCP-tool routing (ADR-0016 case C) as keeping v1 commit 855e330d's matcher for all agents including Gemini, with no carve-out. TECH-SPEC.md:198 already flags this as broken for Gemini but marks it '[V] by source; not yet verified with a live Gemini run', and S-NAMES (TECH-SPEC.md:397) lists it as an open question.
findings.evidence: v1 src/adapters/gemini-cli/hooks.ts:52-64 (cm-main HEAD): EXTERNAL_MCP_MATCHER_PATTERN = 'mcp__(?!.*context-mode)', built on the stated assumption that Gemini's wire shape is 'mcp__<server>__<tool>' (double underscore). I read current Gemini CLI HEAD directly: scratchpad/gemini-cli/packages/core/src/tools/mcp-tool.ts:37 'export const MCP_TOOL_PREFIX = "mcp_";' (single underscore), line ~328 'generateValidName(`${serverName}${MCP_QUALIFIED_NAME_SEPARATOR}${serverToolName}`)' with MCP_QUALIFIED_NAME_SEPARATOR = '_' (single char), and generateValidName() at ~725 unconditionally forces a single 'mcp_' prefix then replaces any char outside [A-Za-z0-9_-.:] with '_'. So the real wire name is 'mcp_<server>_<tool>' with single underscores throughout. The regex 'mcp__(?!.*context-mode)' requires a literal double underscore right after 'mcp', which never occurs in this string. The matcher is structurally unable to match ANY MCP tool name on current Gemini CLI, not just an edge case. This is not a live-probe question -- it is provable from the string-building code alone, so TECH-SPEC's '[U]'/'not yet verified' framing undersells a certainty.
findings.archaeology: INTRODUCED_BY: 3900db8c 'feat(gemini-cli): route external MCP tools through PreToolUse (closes #529 partial — gemini-cli)' (cm-main). ORIGINAL_INTENT (hooks.ts comment, v1): 'Gemini CLI MCP wire shape: mcp__<server>__<tool> (verified in hooks/core/tool-naming.mjs)... Without it, large payloads from slack/telegram/gdrive/notion-style MCPs bypass the routing nudge and flood the model's context.' The v1 fix was written against an older/incorrect belief about Gemini's naming and was apparently never re-verified against a Gemini HEAD that enforces the single-underscore, generateValidName()-sanitized format. REGRESSION_RISK: if v2 ports 855e330d's pattern unchanged for Gemini (as Q1 literally says to do), the context-flood protection ADR-0016 case C exists to provide never engages on Gemini for any external MCP server -- the exact flooding scenario #529 was written to stop. SAFE_FIX_CONSTRAINTS: the Gemini matcher must be rewritten against the real format 'mcp_<server>_<tool>' (and must also handle generateValidName's non-alnum-to-underscore collapsing of the server/tool names themselves, so a server name containing '-' changes the literal string); it cannot reuse a 'mcp__' substring test.
findings.fix: Treat this as an exception to Q1, not a reopening of it: add a Gemini-specific external-MCP matcher derived from mcp-tool.ts's generateValidName() behavior (prefix 'mcp_', single-'_' join, non [A-Za-z0-9_-.:] chars collapsed to '_'), and add a GP3 case asserting it matches a real generated name for an external server. Update TECH-SPEC.md:198/397 from '[U]'/'not yet verified' to '[V] confirmed by source read of mcp-tool.ts current HEAD' so the open S-NAMES item can close without a live run being a blocker.

findings.title: ADR-0011's Antigravity-shares-this-dir claim for Gemini cleanup is correct and already verifiable from source -- confirming, not disputing, this one
findings.claim: ADR-0011:64 says Gemini's data dir ~/.gemini/context-mode/ must be deleted only after a prompt 'because Antigravity shares this dir'.
findings.evidence: Checked against source: src/adapters/antigravity/index.ts:11 (header comment) states 'Session dir: ~/.gemini/context-mode/sessions/' for the Antigravity (non-CLI) adapter -- the same path Gemini CLI uses. This claim is accurate and does not need a finding; recorded here only so Pass B does not re-flag it as unverified.

notes: Scope: Gemini CLI hooks, tool names, install/update/rollback, compaction, deny/rewrite/replace, subagent handling, project source, skills, v1 footprint. Most Gemini-specific claims in README/TECH-SPEC/ADR-0001/0004/0007/0009/0010/0011/0013/0016 were checked against current Gemini CLI HEAD source (scratchpad/gemini-cli) and v1 history (scratchpad/cm-main) and found accurate (PreCompress/SessionStart hook events exist in current HEAD matching ADR-0009's compaction model; MCP tool-name formats for ctx_execute per-row in TECH-SPEC:187-194 match source; Antigravity shared-dir claim confirmed). The one real gap is GEM-B1: Q1's blanket 'keeps v1 #529' instruction does not carve out the Gemini exception that TECH-SPEC itself already documents as broken, and I was able to upgrade that from 'not yet verified' to confirmed-by-source.
